questions.stem: Which of the following is not seen in the human body?
questions.solutionHtml:
L-fructose
  • L-fructose is not seen in the human body
    • All sugars in our body are D-sugars.
    • All amino acids in human proteins are L-amino acids.
    • But there are exceptions. (L-sugar found in the human body, i.e. L-fucose.)


Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 155

questions.stem: Glucuronic acid and Iduronic acid are oxidation products of glucose and idose sugar and are structural components of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). They are which of the following kind of isomers?
questions.solutionHtml:
Epimers
  • Epimers are stereoisomers that differ in configuration around a single asymmetric carbon other than the anomeric carbon.
  • Glucuronic acid and Iduronic acid are C-5 epimers
  • Epimers of glucose can be remembered as MAGI.
    • Mannose -C2 epimer,
    • Allose -C3 epimer,
    • Galactose -C4 epimer
    • Idose -C5 epimer.





Lehninger Biochemistry 6th Edition Page No. 247

questions.stem: An adult male patient of age 50 years was brought to the medical center. The patient complained of swelling in the feet, legs, and face past 6 months and decreased urine output. The patient gave a history of diabetes mellitus for the past 10 years. After a thorough examination, it was decided to assess the functioning status of the kidneys. A compound of which of the following group of compounds can be used for assessing the glomerular filtration rate?
questions.solutionHtml:
Fructosan

Inulin

  • Homopolysaccharide of fructose (Fructan).
  • Source - garlic, onion
  • Neither absorbed nor secreted by renal tubules.
  • Inulin clearance: Ideal for measuring Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR). It is a chemically inert substance and is not metabolized in the It is freely filtered by kidneys. Inulin is administered intravenously to assess the glomerular filtration rate in the patients
  • Also used as a prebiotic (food for bacteria)



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 152

questions.stem: Sucrose-rich medium is inoculated with Gram+ bacteria named Leuconostoc mesenteroides which cause the formation of a compound called Dextran. All of the following are true about dextran, EXCEPT:Highly branchedHomopolymerPartially digested product of starchAlso known as dextrinIt remains in the vascular compartment, therefore works as a volume expanderSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 & 3 are correct
  • Statements: C and D. Dextrins, Partially digested product of starch

Dextrins

  • It consists of a partially digested product of starch or glycogen
  • For example, glycogen when acted upon by α-amylase produces shorter chain glucose polysaccharides known as limit dextrins
  • They have α(1-4) and α(1-6) linkages between glucose residues
  • Other kinds of dextrins are maltodextrins and cyclodextrins



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 148

questions.stem: All of the following are the features of glycoproteins, except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Presence of disaccharide repeat unit
  • The presence of a disaccharide repeating unit is a feature of proteoglycans and not glycoproteins.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 155

questions.stem: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) are polymers made of amino sugars and uronic acid derivatives. Which one of the following GAGs does not contains uronic acid or its derivative?
questions.solutionHtml:
Keratan sulfate
  • Most heterogenous GAG and only GAG without uronic acid
  • Repeating disaccharide unit: N-Acetyl Glucosamine 6-Sulfate + D-Galactose
  • Present in Cornea (Type I Keratan Sulfate), and Cartilage (Type II Keratan Sulfate)
  • Responsible for Transparency of cornea



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 608-609

questions.stem: All of the following are true regarding proteoglycans, EXCEPT:

options.label: B
options.text: They hold less amount of water

options.label: C
options.text: They are made up of sugar and amino acids

questions.answerText: They hold less amount of water
questions.solutionHtml:
They hold less amount of water

Option: B.  They hold less amount of water

  • Proteoglycans are negatively charged due to the presence of a large number of acetyl, carboxyl, and sulfate groups. Due to these charges, they can form a large number of hydrogen bonds with water and thus they can hold a large amount of water.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd edition, page no. 608-609

questions.stem: Which of the following statement regarding carbohydrates is NOT CORRECT?

options.label: A
options.text: The parent carbohydrate which gives rise to other carbohydrates is Glycerol

options.label: B
options.text: The minimum number of carbons possible in carbohydrates is 3.

options.label: C
options.text: The minimum number of ‘OH’ groups possible in carbohydrates is 2.

options.label: D
options.text: The minimum number of functional groups possible in carbohydrates is 1.

questions.answerText: The parent carbohydrate which gives rise to other carbohydrates is Glycerol
questions.solutionHtml:
The parent carbohydrate which gives rise to other carbohydrates is Glycerol.
  • The carbohydrate which gives rise to other carbohydrates is D-Glyceraldehyde (not Glycerol).
  • D-Glyceraldehyde is the simplest carbohydrate that exists.
  • Glycerol is the parent alcohol for glycerolipids.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 147-149

questions.stem: Chitin is a homopolysaccharide present abundantly in the exoskeleton of insects and the cell wall of fungi. Which of the following is a component of Chitin?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucosamine

Chitin

  • A homopolysaccharide made up of N-Acetyl Glucosamine connected in β(1 → 4) linkage.
  • Second most abundant polysaccharide in nature after cellulose




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 154

questions.stem: A patient of 24-year of age presents symptoms of polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia. The urine sample of the patient was tested with Benedict’s test. Brick red precipitate developed in the urine sample. The principle of the test involves a reaction:
questions.solutionHtml:
Reduction of Cu++ ions
  • The reducing sugars like glucose in urine catalyzes the reduction of cupric ions in Benedict’s solution into cuprous ions to form red-colored The reducing sugars are oxidized in the reaction.
  • Benedict’s test can also be used to check for the presence of glucose in a urine Since this test detects any aldehydes and α-hydroxy ketones and glucose is an aldose whose open-chain forms an aldehyde group, the test yields a positive result when glucose is present in the analyte.
  • However, a positive reaction can also be given by the presence of ascorbic acid, homogentisic acid, and other reducing substances in urine. Therefore, a positive Benedict’s test does not necessarily imply that the test subject is diabetic.




Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 249

questions.stem: Cellulose is the most abundant organic molecule on earth mainly present in the cell walls of plants and also fungi. Chemically, it is a:
questions.solutionHtml:
Non-starch polysaccharide

Option: B. Cellulose

  • unbranched, non-starch homopolysaccharide
  • It is made up of glucose molecules linked by beta (1→ 4) glycosidic linkages. This linkage can't be broken down by any human enzyme due to beta anomerism at C-1.
  • Intestinal bacteria ferments cellulose into short-chain fatty acid (Butyrate). 



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 608-609

questions.stem: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) due to their chemical nature provide cushioning and lubricating properties to the tissues. Which GAG is present in the cornea?
questions.solutionHtml:
Keratan Sulfate

Option: D.  Keratan Sulfate

Glycosaminoglycan in the cornea:

  • Keratan sulfate (KS) >>> Chondroitin sulfate (CS) & Dermatan sulfate (DS)
  • All are present in the cornea, but KS is in the maximum amount
  • Immunohistochemistry revealed the presence of both high- and low-sulfated epitopes of KS, as well as DS, throughout the cornea
  • CS is present only in the peripheral cornea before the limbus.
  • Keratan sulfate is also responsible for corneal transparency.
  • Keratan Sulfate-I is present in the cornea while Keratan Sulfate-II is present in cartilages.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 608-609

questions.stem: The enzyme alpha-amylase secreted by the pancreas digests starch into which of the following major products?
questions.solutionHtml:
Limit dextrins, maltose, and maltotriose
  • Alpha-amylase secreted by the pancreas digests starch into Limit dextrins, maltose, and maltotriose

Complete hydrolysis of starch is done by salivary and pancreatic amylases as:





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 528

questions.stem: Sugars generally exhibit isomerism due to the presence of asymmetric carbons. Which of the following sugars has no asymmetric carbon?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dihydroxyacetone

Asymmetric carbon: When carbon is attached to four different atoms or group of atoms

  • Any compound having asymmetric carbon shows both structural and optical isomerism.
  • Carbohydrates and amino acids have asymmetric carbon so, both structural and optical isomerism are present.
  • The number of Asymmetric carbons is always one less in keto form as compared to aldehyde form.
  • Dihydroxyacetone is the only carbohydrate that has no asymmetric carbon




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 149

questions.stem: Sugars are reducing in nature and get readily oxidized to form acids. The oxidation of sugar Galactose with a strong oxidizing agent produces:
questions.solutionHtml:
Mucic Acid

Oxidation of sugars with acid forms sugar acids

  • In mild oxidation, either C1 is oxidized or C6 is oxidized
    • If the Aldehyde group (C1) is oxidized, then Aldonic Acid is produced.
    • If the last carbon (C6) is oxidized, then Uronic Acid is produced
    • Under strong acid, both the first and last carbon of sugar is oxidized to form Saccharic Acid



Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 250

questions.stem: Isomerism in sugars provides them with characteristic physical and chemical properties. Sugar enantiomers are isomers that differ in structure at which carbon:
questions.solutionHtml:
Penultimate Carbon

Enantiomers

  • Also known as mirror images of each other e.g. D-and L-Glyceraldehyde and D-glucose and L-glucose.
  • If at penultimate carbon -OH is on right it is given the designation as D isomer and if -OH is on left it is given the designation as L isomer (See fig below).
  • Note: As seen in glucose, the orientation of -H and -OH changes at all of the chiral carbons but for giving D- and L- notations, we look at the penultimate carbon/2nd last carbon. That’s why it is also known as reference carbon.





Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 149

questions.stem: Features of Hyaluronic acid is/ are:Longest glycosaminoglycanN-acetyl galactosamineHas glucuronic acidN-acetyl neuraminic acidIduronic acidSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
1 & 3 are correct

Hyaluronic acid

  • longest GAG
  • made up of N-acetyl glucosamine + D-glucuronic acid as repeating unit
  • does not contain any sulfate.
  • forms clear, highly viscous, non-compressible solutions that serve as a lubricant
  • provides tensile strength and elasticity.
  • present in synovial fluid & vitreous humor.



Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, 7th Edition, Page No. 259

questions.stem: The majority of calories in our diet are derived from carbohydrates, which can contain a variety of glycosidic bonds. Which one of the following carbohydrates contains glucosyl units linked through α-1,6 glycosidic bonds?
questions.solutionHtml:
Amylopectin

Option: B.

  • The starch amylopectin is a branched polysaccharide of glucosyl units linked through α-1,4 glycosidic bonds with α-1,6 glycosidic bonds as branch points.
  • The straight-chained starch amylose and the disaccharide maltose are both linked through α-1,4 glycosidic bonds.







Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 152

questions.stem: Case: A 54-year-old woman who was bed bound in a nursing home began to develop swelling in her left leg. She was diagnosed with a Venous Doppler ultrasound and was found to have a deep vein thrombosis.Lead Question: She should be treated with which chemical to prevent the clot from enlarging.
questions.solutionHtml:
Heparin
  • Heparin is a naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan or proteoglycan with the repeating disaccharide containing glucosamine (GlcN) and either of the two uronic acids.
  • Heparin is usually stored within the secretory granules of mast cells and released only into the vasculature at sites of tissue injury. Heparin binds specifically to lipoprotein lipase present in capillary walls, causing a release of this enzyme into circulation.
  • Heparin is also used as an anticoagulant that binds to antithrombin and activates it, which in turn inactivates thrombin. Thus, heparin will prevent the clot from enlarging in this patient. Heparin is also used for laboratory techniques involving the estimation of blood pH, Blood gases, Electrolytes, and Ionized calcium.




Lippincott Illustrated Reviews Biochemistry 7th Edition Page No. 164

questions.stem: A 7-month-old boy with coarse facial features, skeletal abnormalities, and delayed growth and development is diagnosed with I-cell disease based on his presentation, and on histologic and biochemical testing. Deficiency of phosphorylating enzymes for the formation of which of the following recognition marker leads to I-cell disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mannose 6 phosphate
  • I-cell disease is a Lysosomal storage disease due to a defect in the gene that initiates the synthesis of the mannose 6-phosphate. The disease occurs due to no phosphorylation of mannose as:
  • This condition is characterized by severe progressive psychomotor retardation and a variety of physical signs, with death often occurring in the first decade of life.
  • Diagnosis: Serum Lysosomal Enzymes ↑↑ (as lysosomal enzymes do not reach lysosomes)




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 562

questions.stem: Which of the following is correct about sucrosea. Alpha-D- glucopyranosyl-(1→2)-β-D- fructofuranosideb. Reducing sugarc. Made up of 13 carbonsd. Invert sugarSelect the correct answer from the given below code:

options.label: A
options.text: Only a, and d are correct

options.label: B
options.text: a, c, and d are correct

options.label: C
options.text: a, b, and c are correct

options.label: D
options.text: All four (a, b, c, & d) are correct

questions.answerText: Only a, and d are correct
questions.solutionHtml:
Only a, and d are correct

Sucrose

  • Produced naturally in plants, which is refined to form table sugar.
  • A solution of sugar is optically active and dextrorotatory.
  • Also known as invert sugar because when sucrose solution is heated, it gives rise to glucose and fructose, and the angle of the specific rotation of the plain polarized light changes (inverted) from positive (for pure sucrose) to a negative value due to the formation of the optical isomers of the mixture of glucose and fructose sugars.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 153

questions.stem: Which of the following statements are true/false about glycosaminoglycans?a. Branched, synthesized in mitochondriab. Tandem repeats of amino sugar and uronic acidc. Component of ECMd. Highly positively chargede. Proteins associated with glycosaminoglycans are called core proteins,Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
a-F, b-T, c-T, d-F, e-T

Statement:  A.  False

  • GAGs are unbranched, and synthesized in ER and Golgi.
  • Hyaluronic acid is the only GAG that is not synthesized by the Golgi apparatus. It is formed at the plasma membrane.

Statement: B. True

  • GAGs are polymers made of tandem repeats of amino sugar and uronic acid
  • These amino sugars present are N acetyl glucosamine and N acetyl galactosamine and are highly sulfated while uronic acids are glucuronic acid and Iduronic acid.
  • Keratan sulfate is only GAG without any uronic acid.

Statement: C. True

  • GAGs are found in ECM.
  • In bone and cartilage, they provide strength and flexibility (Hyaluronic acid, Chondroitin Sulfate)
  • In the eyes they are responsible for the transparency of the cornea (keratan sulfate)
  • Heparin is the only GAG that is present intracellularly.

Statement: D. False

  • GAGs are highly sulfated and have number of carboxy, sulfate and acetyl group which provide a large negative charge on them.
  • The repulsion of these charges makes them slimy and slippery.
  • Due to these charges, GAGs can hold a lot of water, so hygroscopic in nature.

Statement: E.  True

  • GAGs are attached to proteins, therefore called Proteoglycans.
  • On the Hyaluronic acid backbone, many core proteins and link proteins are attached.
  • Linear GAG chains of Amino sugars and Uronic acid (tandem repeats) are covalently attached to core proteins by a core trisaccharide (Galactose-Galactose-Xylose).



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 637

questions.stem: Benedict's test is a semi-quantitative test and gives an idea of the quantity of sugar present depending on the Color. Which color in Benedict’s test indicates that no sugar is present?
questions.solutionHtml:
Blue
  • Benedict's reagent contains Cupric (Cu2+) ions which give blue color to the solution. They are stabilized to cupric form by sodium citrate.
  • Reducing sugars can donate H (e-) to these cupric ions to reduce them to cuprous (Cu1+) which combines with oxygen to form cuprous oxide (CuO) which forms small to large size starch.
  • The color of these CuO precipitates depends on the size and is either yellow (small size ppt) or Red (large size ppt).
  • Depending on the amount of red CuO formed, we will see different colors in the tube. But these colors can only tell the approximate amount of sugar. So, it’s a semi-quantitative test.
  • If there is no reducing sugar present in the sample, the original blue color will be retained in the tube after heating.



Manual of Practical Biochemistry by Rafi Mohammed 3rd Edition, Page No. 4

questions.stem: A cataract is a dense cloudy area formed in the lens of the eye. The excess accumulation of which of the following in the eye most certainly will result in a cataract?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sugar alcohol

Sugar alcohols and cataract:

  • Reduction of monosaccharides forms sugar alcohols
  • sugar alcohols are hygroscopic, absorb water, and will cause cell swelling
  • They especially get accumulated in the lens of the eye causing cataract.

Examples:

  • Glucose forms sorbitol in diabetes and leads to the formation of snowflake cataract
  • In galactosemia, excess galactose is reduced to galactitol and give rise to oil-drop cataract




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 200

questions.stem: A child's developmental progress stopped at 2 years and he also developed coarse facial features. Skeletal deformities started to appear over the next year. Laboratory examination showed glycosaminoglycans in the child's urine. All of the following are associated with Glycosaminoglycans EXCEPT-
questions.solutionHtml:
Transport of lipids
  • Transport of lipids in the blood is done by lipoproteins g. VLDL, LDL, and chylomicrons.
  • Lipoproteins have lipid present in the core and proteins in the periphery to provide a hydrophilic surface which makes them travel easily through the aqueous medium of blood.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 609-610

questions.stem: Cellulose is a plant polysaccharide and is considered dietary fiber in the human diet as it cannot be digested in humans. Cellulose is not broken due to beta-anomerism at:
questions.solutionHtml:
C1

Anomers

  • Isomers with different –H and –OH orientation around the functional carbon.
  • C1 is the functional carbon in glucose or hexoses.
  • Two types of anomers are possible due to this orientation:
    • Alpha (α) - at functional carbon, –OH is downwards
    • Beta (β)- at functional carbon, –OH is upwards
  • β-anomers can't be broken in the body due to the absence of enzymes to break a beta bond.
  • Cellulose is made up of glucose joined by β (1→4) glycosidic bond
  • In glucose functional carbon is at C1 (Aldehyde). So, we can say cellulose is not broken due to β-anomerism at C1.




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd edition, page no. 149, 154

questions.stem: A person after ingesting dairy products feels very uncomfortable with problems of flatulence and distension of his stomach due to gas formation. These symptoms do not appear when he completely avoids any dairy products in his diet. The most likely cause of these symptoms is a deficiency of which of the following conversions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Lactose to glucose + galactose
  • The patient has abdominal discomfort & diarrhea after taking milk and the alleviation of these symptoms on the removal of milk from the diet indicates that the patient is suffering from Lactose Intolerance.
  • It is caused by a deficiency of the β-Galactosidase enzyme aka Lactase which breaks down milk sugar lactose into glucose and galactose which can be easily absorbed.
  • Due to a defect in this enzyme lactose is not broken and accumulates in the intestine which is further fermented by intestinal bacteria producing acid and gas.



Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 528

questions.stem: The number of isomers possible for Glucose are:
questions.solutionHtml:
16
  • The number of isomers possible for a sugar = 2n where; n= number of asymmetric carbons in the linear structure of the molecule.

Note: Do not use extra asymmetric carbon in cyclic structures in this formula.

  • For a ketohexose such as fructose, n= 3 so isomers possible are 23 = 8




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No.149

questions.stem: A male infant who is failing to thrive showed hepatomegaly and splenomegaly, among other findings on examination. Dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate were also present in urine. The patient is suspected to have Hurler syndrome. The enzyme you would select to be assayed to support your diagnosis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
α-L-Iduronidase
  • An absence of α-L-iduronidase occurs in both Hurler’s syndrome and Scheie’s syndrome leading to the accumulation of heparan and dermatan sulfate.
  • However, Scheie’s syndrome is less severe, with corneal clouding, joint degeneration, and increased heart disease.

 




Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry, 32nd Edition, Page No. 611

questions.stem: A 3-year-old boy presents with mental retardation, dysostosis multiplex, and coarse facial feature. There was no corneal clouding seen. The pediatric resident asked the new intern to take a detailed history and present the case. Pedigree chart analysis shows an X-linked recessive pattern. Which of the following biochemical abnormality is the most likely cause of symptoms in this child?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hunter’s disease
  • In this pedigree chart, females are carriers, and males are affected, So it is an X-linked Recessive disorder.
  • Hunter disease: affects males, no corneal clouding.
  • All MPS are inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, except Hunter’s disease, which is inherited in an X-linked recessive manner.



Harper's, Illustrated Biochemistry 32nd Edition, Page No. 611

questions.stem: In a patient’s blood serum increased activity of hyaluronidase is found. A connective tissue pathology will be confirmed by the determination of which of the following compound in his blood serum?
questions.solutionHtml:
Sialic acid
  • The extracellular matrix of connective tissues is rich in hyaluronic acid. Some bacterial and viral pathogens produce hyaluronidase as a means of using hyaluronan as a carbon source and as a possible virulence factor.
  • Hyaluronidases are hyaluronoglucosidases i.e. they cleave the (1→4)-linkages between N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronate. The released N-acetylglucosamine can be converted to sialic acid by the action of two bacterial enzymes first by an epimerase to form N-acetylglucosamine-6-P and then by aldolase by transfer of three carbons from pyruvate to form sialic acid (N-acetyl neuraminic acid).
  • The other product which can be detected in serum will be glucuronic acid.



Textbook of Medical Biochemistry by Dinesh Puri 3rd Edition Page No. 30-31

questions.stem: A routine examination of the urine of an asymptomatic pediatric patient showed a positive reaction with Clinitest (a copper reduction method of detecting reducing sugars), but a negative reaction to the glucose oxidase test. Which one of the following sugars is least likely to be present (assuming a single elevated saccharide):
questions.solutionHtml:
Sucrose
  • Sugars may be called reducing or non-reducing based on their ability to reduce copper during Benedict’s test.
  • The reducing property of sugar is based on the presence of free aldehyde or ketone group in them.
  • Most monosaccharides and disaccharides are reducing sugars, while Sucrose & Trehalose is a non-reducing sugar.
  • In contrast to reducing sugars, sucrose & trehalose do not contain free anomeric carbon atoms therefore a non-reducing sugar.

 





Essentials of Biochemistry, 5th Edition, Page No. 12
